summary: User requests event-driven workflow state persistence triggered by WorkflowTaskCompleted events to replace inefficient polling, achieving real-time state updates with better resource utilization.
userImpact: Users need efficient real-time persistence of workflow state to external databases and currently face high latency and resource waste with polling-based solutions.
proposedFix: Implement event-driven persistence by subscribing to WorkflowTaskCompleted events, querying workflows via QueryWorkflow, and persisting to database. Requires reliable event subscription mechanism and Java SDK code samples.
workaround: Periodically query running workflows via @QueryMethod using a scheduled poller and write results to database
keyQuote: Listen for WorkflowTaskCompleted events from an external service (indicating workflow state may have changed). Query the corresponding workflow via QueryWorkflow (calling its @QueryMethod) to fetch the latest state.
